  • the language menu, a globe with the name of the current language: choose another one and the interface changes at once;
  • the ? menu: Commands lists every command at the command line (as typing help), and About shows the version, the licence and the credits.

? ▸ Help (F1) opens this manual, in the language of the interface, in the browser. F1 opens the page of what you are doing: the open dialog, the ribbon button under the mouse (its tip ends with Press F1 for more information) or the active tool.

Right-click a ribbon tool and choose Add to Quick Access Toolbar: the tool joins the toolbar and starts from there whatever tab is open. Right-click any tool of the toolbar, the default ones included, for Remove from Quick Access Toolbar or Add Separator (a line to its right). The small arrow at the end of the toolbar, Customize Quick Access Toolbar, lists the default tools: tick one to show it again, untick it to remove it. In the same menu, Customize Quick Access Toolbar… opens a window with the toolbar's tools in order: Move Up and Move Down move the one selected left or right, Add Separator puts a line after it, Remove takes it (or a line) away, OK applies. Show below the Ribbon moves the whole toolbar under the ribbon (or above it again). The toolbar is kept for the next sessions. On the ribbon's tabs and in the quick access toolbar each command has its own icon.

docs.title: Ribbon
docs.text:
The ribbon groups the tools in tabs, and each tab in panels. The name of a panel is written under its buttons. A button whose name is followed by a small mark opens a menu. Resting the mouse on a button shows what it does and, in brackets, the shortcut you can type to start it.

Tab Panels Home Select, Build, Circulation, Room & Area, Datum Annotate Select, Dimension, Text, Detail, Tag View Create, Graphics, Sheet Composition, Windows Manage Settings, Inquiry Edit The contextual tab: its panels depend on the active tool and on the selection

Press and release Alt, or press F10, to show the key tips: a letter on every tab (I, N, A, V, G, M, from the first tab to the contextual one) and, on the buttons of the open tab, the shortcut of their tool. Type a tab's letter to open it, then a button's letters to start its tool; Esc hides the key tips. While they show, what you type does not go to the command line.

docs.title: The Home tab
docs.text:
Panel Buttons Select Modify: ends the active tool and goes back to selecting, Esc Build Wall WA, Door DR, Window WN, Roof RF, Flooring SB, Component CM, Curtain Grid CG, Mullion MU Circulation Railing RA, Stairs ST Room & Area Room RM, Separation RS, Area ▾ (Area Plan, Area Boundary Line, Area), Legend LG, Settings ▾ (Area and Volume Computations, Color Schemes) Datum Level: drawn in an elevation or a section, two clicks at the new level's height (from a plan it opens an elevation); Grid GR

Area Boundary Line and Area work in an area plan: until one is open they are greyed, and their tip says to open an area plan first.

docs.title: The Annotate tab
docs.text: Panel Buttons Select Modify Dimension Aligned DI, Linear DL, Angular DA Text Text TX Detail Detail line, Filled region, Masking region, Detail component CD, Repeating detail RD, Insulation IS Tag Tag All TG

docs.title: The View tab
docs.text:
Panel Buttons Create 3D View ▾ (Default 3D View, Save View), Plan Views ▾ (Floor Plan, Area Plan), Duplicate View ▾ (Duplicate, Duplicate with Detailing), Section SE, Elevation EL, Detail DT (a callout), Drafting view VD, Schedules ▾ (Schedule/Quantities, Predefined schedules) Graphics Visibility/Graphics VG, Filters, View templates, and two small buttons: Apply template to current view, Create template from current view Sheet Composition Sheet: a new sheet with the title block you choose; View: places a view on the open sheet Windows Switch Windows, Replicate, Cascade, Tile, Maximize, Close Hidden, User Interface

Save View works only while a 3D view is open, Duplicate with Detailing only for views that are not 3D, and Sheet Composition ▸ View only while a sheet is open.

docs.title: The Manage tab
docs.text:
Panel Buttons Settings Materials, Project information, Object styles, Line styles, Purge unused, Project units UN, Snap, and Additional settings (Line styles, Fill patterns) Inquiry Check: checks the openings and references of the model and reports at the command line

Snap turns snapping on and off for the whole program: it is highlighted while on.

docs.title: The contextual tab
docs.text:
When you start a tool or select something, the ribbon switches by itself to the last tab, which takes the name of what you are doing: Edit | Place Wall while drawing walls, Edit | Walls with walls selected, Edit | Multi-Select with elements of different categories. The tab is marked with its own colour. When the tool ends, or the selection is cleared, the ribbon goes back to the tab you were using.

It always has these panels:

Panel Buttons Select Modify Properties Properties: shows or hides the Properties palette; Type Properties: the properties of the type of the selection, or of the next element the tool will place Modify Seventeen small tools in three rows: Align AL, Offset OF, Mirror - Pick Axis MM, Mirror - Draw Axis DM, Split Element SL, Split with Gap SG; Move MV, Copy CO, Rotate RO, Trim/Extend to Corner TR, Trim/Extend Single Element, Trim/Extend Multiple Elements; Array AR, Scale RE, Pin PN, Unpin UP, Delete (Del)

Delete works only when something is selected. The selecting and modifying chapter describes the Modify tools.

Other panels appear for what is selected or for the tool:

When Panel and buttons Anything selected Selection: Filter (see Selecting and modifying) Doors or windows selected Opening: Flip facing, Flip hand Walls selected Modify Wall: Attach Top (the walls rise to the roof above them), Detach Top A level selected View: Open plan Sections or elevations selected Section: Split Segment (sections only), Flip, Go to View A callout selected Detail: Go to View Curtain walls selected Curtain Wall: Curtain Grid, Mullion, Panel Flooring or Roof tool Draw: Boundary Line, Pick Walls Stairs or Railing tool Mode: Finish Edit Mode; Draw: Run or Lines Mullion tool Placement: Grid Line, Grid Line Segment, All Grid Lines A detail tool The drawing shapes of the tool

docs.title: Options bar
docs.text:
Under the ribbon, the options bar starts with the name of the contextual tab, then shows the settings of the active tool. They apply to the next elements you place. At its end, while a tool is active, it shows the level you are working on: Level: Ground Floor.

Tool Settings on the options bar Wall Height or Depth; the level the wall reaches, or Unconnected with its value; Location Line; Chain; Offset; Radius (greyed: curved walls are not available yet); Exterior on the left or Exterior on the right (the space bar swaps them) Roof The shape: Gable, Hip or Flat; Slope, from 5° to 60°; Overhang, up to 2 m Stairs Width, in millimetres; Railing Type, or None Dimensions What the cursor picks first on a wall: Wall centerlines or Wall faces Detail (callout) The scale of the new detail view, or Reference other view and the detail or drafting view the callout points at (always on in a drafting view) Area Boundary Line Line or Pick lines; with Pick lines, Apply area rules or an Offset Tools that draw lines Ortho (Shift): horizontal and vertical segments only; Snap: snapping to endpoints, midpoints and intersections

With Ortho (Shift) off, holding Shift while drawing gives the same constraint; with it on, Shift releases it.

Right-click the options bar and choose Dock at Bottom to move it just above the status bar; Dock at Top brings it back. The choice is kept for the next sessions.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
The Properties palette shows and changes the parameters of what you are working on. From top to bottom it has:

  • the type selector: the family in small letters and the type underneath. Click it to choose another type: the selected elements change type, or, while a tool is active, the next element gets that type;
  • a row with what the palette is showing, for example Walls (1) or New Wall, and the Edit Type button, which opens the type properties;
  • the parameters, in groups (Constraints, Graphics, Identity Data…). Click the name of a group to fold it. Values in grey are read-only: they are computed from the model;
  • the Apply button, which confirms a value you are typing. Enter does the same.

What the palette shows depends on the situation:

Situation The palette shows Nothing selected, no tool The properties of the active view (scale, detail level, visual style…), or of the view clicked in the Project Browser A tool active The type of the next element, as New Wall, New Door… One element selected Its type and its instance parameters Several elements of one category Their number, as Walls (3) Elements of different categories Multi-Select, Common (5), and how many of each category, as 3 × Walls

Lengths are written and read in the project's units (millimetres in a new project). You can type a value with its unit, for example 2.7m.

To close the palette, click × on its title; to show it again, use View ▸ Windows ▸ User Interface ▸ Properties or the Properties button of the contextual tab.

docs.title: Project Browser
docs.text:
The Project Browser lists the views, schedules, sheets and families of the project in a tree. Its title carries the name of the project. Click ⊟ or ⊞ to fold or unfold a branch.

Branch What it contains Views (all) ▸ Floor Plans The floor plans of every level, from the lowest, and the callouts drawn in plans Views (all) ▸ Area Plans (…) The area plans, one branch per area scheme Views (all) ▸ Sections, Elevations The sections and the elevations Views (all) ▸ Detail Views The callouts drawn in sections Views (all) ▸ 3D Views {3D}, the default 3D view, and the saved 3D views Views (all) ▸ Drafting views The drafting views Schedules/Quantities The project's schedules, then the predefined schedules Sheets (all) The sheets, as number - name Families The types of the project, by category: walls, doors, windows, floors, roofs, components and the others

The branches of area plans, sections, elevations, detail views and drafting views appear only when they have something in them. The active view is written in bold.

With a view:

  • a click shows its properties in the Properties palette, without opening it;
  • a double-click opens it;
  • a right-click opens its menu: Open, Close (closes its windows), Duplicate View ▸ (Duplicate, Duplicate with Detailing), Apply view template…, Create view template from view…, Delete, Rename…, Properties.

The menu of a sheet has Apply view template to all views… instead of the two template items, and no Duplicate View. {3D} cannot be deleted or renamed.

With a schedule of the project, a click selects it, a double-click opens it, and the right-click menu has Open, Schedule Properties… and Delete. A predefined schedule opens with a click.

With a type, under Families, a double-click opens its type properties; the right-click menu has Type Properties, Duplicate…, Create Instance (starts the tool that places it, with that type) and Delete.

After a click in the Project Browser, the keyboard moves in it: Up and Down go from row to row (the view's properties show in the palette), Right opens a branch, Left closes it or goes up to the branch the row is in, Enter opens the view.

Views go on sheets from here too. Drag a plan, section, elevation, drafting view, legend, saved 3D view or schedule onto the open sheet: its viewport follows the cursor and stays where you drop it. Or drop it on a sheet's name in the tree: the sheet opens and the viewport follows the cursor until you click. While you drag, the tree scrolls when the cursor nears its edge. The right-click menu of a sheet has Add View…. A view already on a sheet is refused, with the reason on the command line; legends and schedules can go on several sheets. A saved 3D view is drawn on the sheet with the edges seen from its camera.

The right-click menu of a plan, section or drafting view has Find Referring Views: the views that show its symbol and the sheets it is on; Go to View opens the one chosen.

docs.title: Drawing area and view windows
docs.text:
Every view you open is a window in the drawing area. A view opened again comes to the front; at least one window always stays open. View ▸ Windows arranges them:

Button What it does Switch Windows Lists the open windows; the active one is ticked Replicate Opens a second window on the active view, with its own zoom Cascade Overlapping windows, each with its title bar: drag a title to move a window, its edges to resize it Tile All the windows side by side, each with a title bar; the active one has a blue title and frame Maximize The active window fills the drawing area; the others wait underneath Close Hidden Closes every window except the active one User Interface Shows or hides the Project Browser, Properties, the Command line, the Status bar and the Navigation bar

Click in a window to make it active: the tools work in the active window, the others only show the model. In Tile and Cascade, the × on a window's title bar closes it.

Tile puts the active window at the top left and the others after it, from the most recently active; Switch Windows lists them in the same order. Tile again after working in another window and that window comes first.

User Interface ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts lists the commands with their shortcuts. Search a command by name, or Filter the list (All, All Defined, All Not Defined, All Reserved); select a command, type the keys in Press new keys and click Assign. Keys that another command already has are refused, with the reason; Remove takes away the keys you added. Your shortcuts are kept for the next sessions and start the command when typed, as the built-in ones do.

A tool never changes the active view by itself. Started in a view where it cannot work (a roof or a room in a 3D view, a level in a plan, an area outside an area plan), it opens Go to View: the views that suit it, with the plan of the active level chosen first. Open View opens the chosen view and starts the tool there; Cancel leaves everything as it was. Edit Boundary of a floor, roof, stair or railing, from a section or an elevation, asks the same way for a plan of its level, and a new section or elevation leaves the plan you drew it in active. Move and Copy also work in sections and elevations, along the view.

docs.title: View control bar
docs.text:
At the bottom of every plan, section, elevation, callout and drafting view:

Control What it does The scale, for example 1 : 100 Opens the list of scales; under Custom type another one, as 1 : 75, and press Enter Detail level Coarse, Medium or Fine Crop View Crops the view to its crop region, or stops cropping; a blue dot shows it is on Show Crop Region Shows or hides the crop region's frame; a blue dot shows it is on Temporary Hide/Isolate Hides or isolates elements or categories in this view until you reset it; framed while active

In a 3D view, the bar has the Visual style (Wireframe, Hidden Line, Shaded, Shaded with Edges, Consistent Colors) and Temporary Hide/Isolate. A sheet has no view control bar: its views have their own scale.

docs.title: Navigation bar
docs.text:
On the right edge of the active view (the left edge in Arabic), three buttons: Zoom to Fit (the same as Home), Zoom In and Zoom Out.

Under them, Zoom Options opens the zoom menu: Zoom in Region (drag a rectangle on the view; Esc gives up), Zoom Out (2x), Zoom to Fit, Zoom All to Fit (every open window), Zoom Sheet Size (the view at the size it prints), and Previous Pan/Zoom and Next Pan/Zoom, which go back and forth through the views of that window. Typed: ZR, ZO, ZF, ZA, ZS, ZP. In a 3D view the last button, SteeringWheels, opens the navigation wheel: drag its Zoom, Orbit or Pan sector; click Center to make the model point under its centre the point the view turns about, or Rewind to go back to the previous view; Close Wheel (×) closes it.

docs.title: Moving around in the views
docs.text:
In plans, sections, elevations and sheets Mouse wheel Zooms in and out at the cursor Drag with the middle button Pans Drag with the left button A selection window, or moves the selected elements (Selecting and modifying) Home Fits the whole view in the window In 3D views Drag with the right button, or Shift + middle button Orbits around the model Drag with the middle button Pans Drag with the left button A selection window, or moves the selected elements Mouse wheel Zooms in and out Home Fits the whole model in the window

A small tripod in the lower corner of the 3D view shows the directions of the axes: X red, Y green, Z blue. A saved 3D view remembers where you left it.

In 3D, the wheel zooms keeping the model point under the cursor in place, and the orbit turns about the centre of the selection, or about the point the view looks at when nothing is selected.

The ViewCube, in the top corner of the 3D view, turns with the model. Click a face (TOP, FRONT, RIGHT…) to look from that side, an edge to look from between two sides, a corner from between three; drag the cube to orbit. The house above it, Home, goes back to the starting view; the letters N, E, S, W under it look from that point of the compass.

docs.title: The context menu of a view
docs.text:
Right-click in a view while no tool is active. If the cursor is on an element that is not selected, the element is selected first. The menu has:

  • Cancel: clears the selection;
  • Select All Instances ▸ Visible in View or ▸ In Entire Project: the elements of the same type; Select Previous: the selection made before;
  • Hide in view ▸ Elements or ▸ Category: hides the selected elements, or their whole categories, in this view;
  • Override graphics in view ▸ By category…: opens Visibility/Graphics on the categories of the selection;
  • Visibility/Graphics….

While a tool is active, a right-click does what Esc does: it cancels the step in progress.

At the top of the menu, Repeat [command] starts the last tool you used again; Enter does the same when no tool is active and the command line is empty. The menu is the same in plans, sections and 3D views.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Under the drawing area, the command line shows the log of what has been done, the most recent at the bottom: the commands run, in grey after a >, their results, and errors in red. On its last row, the prompt says what the active tool expects, for example WALL next point [Esc to finish]:, or Command: when no tool is active.

You do not need to click it: whatever you type while no field is being edited goes to the command line. Enter runs the line; Up and Down bring back the lines typed before. The command line chapter describes the commands.

docs.title: Status bar
docs.text:
On the left, the status bar shows:

  • while a tool is active, what the tool expects (the same prompt as the command line);
  • with no tool, the category and the type of the element under the cursor, as Walls : Exterior wall - Clay block 300 + ETICS;
  • while you drag, the length of the move, as Move: 1500;
  • otherwise a reminder of the mouse: Click: select · Ctrl: add · Shift: remove · Wheel: zoom · Middle: pan in plans, Click: select · Right: orbit · Middle: pan · Wheel: zoom in 3D.

On the right, the number of selected elements and a funnel: click the number to open Filter. Then Select and Drag, which lets you drag elements without selecting them first; in a plan, also the coordinates of the cursor in metres.

docs.title: Selecting, in short
docs.text:
The selecting and modifying chapter describes selection in full. The essentials:

  • click an element to select it; click an empty point to clear the selection;
  • Ctrl + click adds an element to the selection, Shift + click takes it out; Tab highlights the next element under the cursor, or a chain of joined walls;
  • drag from left to right to select what is entirely inside the rectangle, from right to left to select what it touches;
  • drag a selected element to move it;
  • Ctrl+A selects the elements of the open plan's level, or of the whole model in a 3D view; Del deletes the selection; Esc clears it.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
BIMopen has two kinds of shortcuts: keys, such as Ctrl+Z, which act at once, and typed shortcuts, such as WA, which you type letter by letter and confirm with Enter, like any command. Typed shortcuts are the same in every language.

On macOS, Cmd takes the place of Ctrl.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key What it does Ctrl+Z Undoes the last change Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z Redoes the change just undone Ctrl+S Saves the project; a project never saved asks for a file name Ctrl+P Opens Print Ctrl+A Selects the elements of the open plan's level, or of the whole model in a 3D view Del Deletes the selected elements, and the elements they host Home Fits the whole view in its window F1 Opens the page of this manual about the open dialog, the ribbon button under the mouse or the active tool Esc Cancels the step in progress; pressed again, ends the tool; with no tool, clears the selection Enter Runs the line typed at the command line; confirms a value in the Properties palette Up / Down At the command line, the lines typed before Space While drawing walls, swaps the exterior and interior side; while placing a component or a detail component, rotates it Shift While drawing, keeps segments horizontal or vertical (or frees them, when Ortho is on); with a click or a window, takes elements out of the selection; while dragging, frees a joined wall or keeps the move horizontal or vertical Ctrl + click Adds an element to the selection; held when a drag starts, places a copy Tab / Shift+Tab Highlights the next (previous) element under the cursor, or a chain of joined walls and lines Ctrl+Left Selects again what was selected before Left Right Up Down Move the selection a small step; with Shift, ten steps

Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+A, Del and Home act on the model only while you are not typing in a field: in a field they act on the text.

In a floor, roof, stair or railing sketch, Esc (or a double-click) also finishes the sketch when it has enough points.

In the Text Note dialog, Ctrl+Enter inserts the note and Esc cancels it.

Alt pressed and released, or F10, shows the ribbon's key tips. With no tool active and nothing typed, Enter repeats the last tool. After a click in the Project Browser, the arrow keys and Enter move in its tree.

docs.title: Mouse
docs.text: In plans and sections In 3D views Wheel Zoom at the cursor Zoom Middle button, drag Pan Pan; with Shift, orbit Left button, drag Selection window (left to right: inside; right to left: touching), or moves the selected elements The same Right button Context menu; with a tool active, cancels the step The same; dragging, orbit Double-click Finishes a sketch –

docs.title: Typed shortcuts
docs.text: Type the letters while no field is being edited, then press Enter. Without arguments, a shortcut starts the tool or opens the dialog; with arguments, it runs the command at once (see Command line and MCP).

docs.title: Modelling
docs.text: Shortcut Command Starts WA or W wall Wall DR door Door WN window Window SB floor Floor (the Flooring button) RF roof Roof CM component Component ST stair Stairs RA railing Railing CG curtaingrid Curtain grid MU mullion Mullion CP curtainpanel Curtain wall panel GR grid Grid RM room Room RS roomsep Room separation PA areaplan The Area Plan dialog CA areaboundary Area boundary line – area Area LG legend Color fill legend SC colorscheme The Color Schemes dialog

docs.title: Modifying
docs.text: Shortcut Command Starts MV or M move Move CO copy Copy RO rotate Rotate MM mirror Mirror - Pick Axis DM mirror Mirror - Draw Axis AR array Array OF offset Offset AL align Align TR trim Trim/Extend to Corner SL split Split Element SG split Split with Gap RE resize Scale PN pin Pins the selection UP unpin Unpins the selection SA selectinstances Selects all instances of the selection's types visible in the view DEL delete Deletes the selection U undo Undoes the last change

docs.title: Annotating and detailing
docs.text:
Shortcut Command Starts DI dim Aligned dimension DL lineardim Linear dimension DA angulardim Angular dimension TX text Text TG tag Tags the untagged doors and windows of the level – detailline Detail line RG region Filled region – mask Masking region CD detailcomponent Detail component RD repeatingdetail Repeating detail IS insulation Insulation

Note

The tip of the Detail line button shows DL, but DL starts the linear dimension, as the tip of Linear says. To start the detail line by typing, use detailline.

docs.title: Views and settings
docs.text:
Shortcut Command Starts or opens SE section Section EL elevation Elevation DT callout Callout (the Detail button) DS splitsegment Split Segment of a section VD draftingview The Drafting view dialog PP floorplan The Floor Plan dialog DV duplicateview Duplicates the active view VG or VV vg Visibility/Graphics WF, HL, SD – Wireframe, Hidden Line, Shaded: the visual style of the active view HH, HI – Hide Element, Isolate Element for now HC, IC – Hide Category, Isolate Category for now HR – Reset Temporary Hide/Isolate EH, VH – Hide in view: the selected elements, their category RH – Reveal Hidden Elements, on and off TL thinlines Thin lines, on and off SO objectstyle Object styles MA material Materials UN units Project units PU purge Purge unused – filter Filters – viewtemplate View templates – applytemplate Apply a view template to the active view – linestyle Line styles – fillpattern Fill patterns – saveview3d Saves the {3D} view with a name – renameview Renames the active view

The commands with – have no short form, but their whole name works the same way. help lists every command and its short forms.

The zoom commands have typed shortcuts too: ZR zoom in region, ZO zoom out (2x), ZF zoom to fit, ZA zoom all to fit, ZS zoom sheet size, ZP previous pan/zoom. View ▸ Windows ▸ User Interface ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts gives any command shortcuts of your own (The interface).

docs.title: Projects and files
docs.text: This chapter describes how a project is created, opened, saved and exchanged with other programs, its settings and the options of BIMopen itself.

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
application menu ➤ New ➤ Project… opens New project:

  • Template file: BIMopen's default template, or the one set in Options ➤ File Locations; a template file chosen with Browse…; or None, which starts from two levels and one type of each kind.
  • Create new: Project or Project Template.

A project made from a template has everything the template had: types, settings, views, sheets, project information and print settings. Saving it asks for a name, so the template is not overwritten.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: A template is a .bimtpl file. application menu ➤ Save As ➤ Template… saves the open project as a template; a project created as a Project Template, or a template opened, is saved as a template too.

docs.title: Opening a project
docs.text:
Ctrl+O, application menu ➤ Open… or Open on the quick access toolbar opens a project. application menu ➤ Recent Documents lists the latest projects, the most recent first; a pin keeps a project in the list. Without a file, BIMopen starts on Recent Files, with the recent projects, Open…, New and the Sample project (unless Enable Recent Files page at startup is unticked in the options). Dropping a project file on the window opens it too.

A project already open in another BIMopen window opens read-only: Save asks for a new name. If BIMopen stopped without saving (a crash, a power cut), opening the project again brings the unsaved work back as unsaved changes.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Ctrl+S, or Save on the quick access toolbar, saves the project; until then the file stays as it was last saved, and the title bar shows an asterisk. application menu ➤ Save As ➤ Project… writes it to a new file and goes on there.

Save As ➤ Options… opens File Save Options: Maximum backups keeps that many earlier versions beside the file (house.0001.bimopen, house.0002.bimopen…), deleting the oldest; Compact file rewrites the file without its obsolete parts at the next save.

When a changed project stays unsaved for the interval set in Options ➤ General (Save reminder interval, 30 minutes to start with), Save Reminder offers to save it, not to save it, or to change the interval.

Before New, Open…, a recent document, the sample project, or closing the window, a changed project asks Save changes to …?: Yes saves it, No drops the changes, Cancel keeps it open.

In the browser, Open… uses the browser's file chooser, and Save downloads the file; backups, crash recovery and read-only opening need a file on disk and are desktop-only.

docs.title: Project information
docs.text: Manage ➤ Settings ➤ Project information sets the project's name, number, client, address, issue date and status: the title blocks of every sheet show them.

docs.title: Project units
docs.text: Manage ➤ Settings ➤ Project units lists the quantities (length, area, volume, angle, slope and the others) with a sample of each, and the Decimal symbol/digit grouping. Format… of a quantity sets its unit, its Rounding (a number of decimals, or Custom with an Increment factor, such as 5 mm), its Unit symbol, Suppress trailing zeros, the plus sign for positive values and digit grouping.

docs.title: Sun Settings
docs.text: Manage ➤ Additional settings ➤ Sun Settings opens the sun settings of the active view, the same as the sun button of the view control bar (see Views and graphics).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
application menu ➤ Options has four tabs; the choices are kept between sessions.

Tab What it sets General The save reminder interval User Interface The theme (Light or Dark), the language, the interface style and size; Enable Recent Files page at startup; the ribbon tab after a selection ends or a tool closes (Stay on the Modify tab or Return to the previous tab) and Display the contextual tab on selection; Tooltip Assistance (None, Minimal, Normal, Extra High) Graphics Invert background color, Selection color, Highlight color, Use anti-aliasing for 3D views, Temporary Dimension Text Appearance (size and background) File Locations Default template file path (the template of New) and Default path for user files (where the file dialogs open)

docs.title: Transferring project standards
docs.text:
Manage ➤ Settings ➤ Transfer Project Standards copies settings from another project into this one. In Select Items To Copy, choose the project with Browse… (Copy from:), then tick what to copy: the types of walls, floors, roofs, doors and windows, stairs, railings, curtain panels and mullions, line styles, filled region types, materials, fill and line patterns, line weights, object styles, view templates, filters, viewport types, title blocks, the project units, the print settings and the project information (Check all, None).

What is copied brings along what it uses: a wall type its materials, a material its patterns, a view template its filters. When names are already in the project, Duplicate Types asks whether to Overwrite them or to transfer the New Only. The whole transfer is one step of undo.

docs.title: Exporting to IFC
docs.text:
application menu ➤ Export ➤ IFC… writes the model in IFC4: walls with their axis and body, openings, doors, windows, floors, roofs, stairs, railings, curtain walls, furniture and rooms as spaces, on their storeys.

Export ➤ Options ➤ IFC Options… opens IFC Export Classes: the IFC class of each category; Not Exported leaves a category out, and Default goes back to the standard classes. The classes are kept with the project.

docs.title: Opening IFC files
docs.text:
application menu ➤ Open ➤ IFC… makes a new project from an IFC2x3 or IFC4 file, in metres or millimetres: storeys become levels, walls are rebuilt from their axis (or from the long side of their body), slabs become floors, doors and windows go in the walls their openings cut, and spaces become rooms. The messages count what was not read.

Open ➤ IFC Options… opens Import IFC Options: what each IFC class becomes (walls, floors, doors, windows, rooms or Not Imported), and Default. The choices are kept between sessions.

docs.title: Revit projects
docs.text: Opening a .rvt file makes a new project from what can be read of it: levels, wall types and walls, doors and windows, floors. The messages say what was approximated.

docs.title: Other exports
docs.text: Printing to PDF and exporting images are described in Sheets, schedules and printing; schedules export as delimited text from the same chapter. bimopen-cli convert exports from the command line (see Command line and MCP).

docs.title: Selecting and modifying
docs.text: Before most changes you select what to change. This chapter describes how elements are highlighted and selected, how a selection is refined, how selected elements are dragged, and the tools of the Modify panel. Everything here works the same in the desktop app and in the browser.

docs.title: Highlighting and selecting
docs.text:
Move the cursor over an element: its lines are drawn wider, the status bar at the bottom of the window names it (category and type, as Walls : Exterior wall…), and after a moment the same words appear under the cursor. Click to select the highlighted element. A selected element is drawn in the selection colour in every view where it shows, and the count at the right end of the status bar says how many elements are selected.

A right click on an element selects it and opens the context menu. Esc, or a click on an empty spot, clears the selection.

To… Do this add an element to the selection Ctrl + click take an element out of the selection Shift + click select what is wholly inside a window drag from left to right select what a window touches drag from right to left (the window is dashed) add, or take away, what a window catches drag with Ctrl, or with Shift select again what was selected before Ctrl+Left, or right click ▸ Select Previous

Windows work in plans, sections, sheets and 3D views. In a 3D view the left button selects; the right button orbits and the middle button pans (see The interface).

docs.title: Elements close together: TAB
docs.text: When elements lie close together or one over the other, the one highlighted may not be the one you want. Keep the cursor still and press Tab: the next element under the cursor is highlighted and the status bar names it. Shift+Tab goes back. Click to select the highlighted element. In a 3D view Tab goes from the nearest element to the ones behind it; on a sheet, through views placed one over the other.

docs.title: Chains of walls and lines
docs.text:
Walls and lines joined end to end form a chain. With the cursor on one of them, Tab highlights the whole chain (the status bar says Chain of n joined elements); a click selects it. A chain can mix walls with room separation lines and area boundaries; detail lines chain with the detail lines of their view. Where three or more meet, the chain goes on along the one that makes the smallest angle with the last; a wall that stops against another one between its ends takes the chain on along that wall.

Part of a chain. Select the first element of the part, move the cursor over the last one and press Tab: the elements between them are highlighted. Tab again highlights the whole chain, a third time the last element alone. Click to select what is highlighted. On a closed chain the part goes round by the side where the cursor is: near the end of the last element that one way round reaches first.

Elements joined at a point. Select an element and keep the cursor on it, near an end where others are joined. Tab highlights it with the nearest one joined there; Tab again, every element joined there. Click to select them.

A selected chain. Where two selected walls or lines meet, a round control appears. Drag it to move the joint: the selected ends there move together and stay joined; elements not selected are left where they are. Drag the chain with Shift to move it whole, horizontally or vertically; drag it with Ctrl to place a copy.

docs.title: Filtering a selection
docs.text: Click the count in the status bar, or Filter on the contextual tab, to open Filter. It lists the categories in the selection, how many elements each has, and the total. Untick a category to leave its elements out: the selection and the count in the status bar follow at once. Check all and Check none tick or untick every category. OK keeps the selection, Cancel brings back the one you started with.

docs.title: Select All Instances
docs.text: Right-click an element ▸ Select All Instances, then Visible in View (the elements of the same type shown in the active view) or In Entire Project. Typing SA and Enter does the same as Visible in View. The element must have a type: rooms, for example, have none.

docs.title: Dragging elements
docs.text:
Drag a selected element to move it; the whole selection moves together, and one drag is undone by one Ctrl+Z. A temporary dimension shows the move, and the status bar its length (Move: 1500). With Select and Drag turned on in the status bar, an element can be dragged without selecting it first; with it off, a drag that starts on an element not selected draws a window.

  • A wall joined at its ends to walls that are not selected moves square to itself only, and the joined walls stretch to stay joined. Walls that stop against it follow too. Hold Shift to move it freely; the joined walls still follow.
  • Any other element moves freely; hold Shift to keep the move horizontal or vertical.
  • Doors and windows move with their wall and keep their place along it. Dragged on their own, they slide along the wall; dropped on another wall, they move into it.
  • Hold Ctrl when you start dragging to place a copy instead.

Elements are dragged in plans, sections and elevations (along the view), on sheets (views), and in 3D views, where they move on the horizontal plane where you grabbed them. The arrow keys move the selection a small step, rounded to a tidy value at the zoom of the view; with Shift, ten steps.

docs.title: The Modify tools
docs.text:
The Modify panel of the contextual tab has three rows: Align, Offset, Mirror - Pick Axis, Mirror - Draw Axis, Split Element, Split with Gap; Move, Copy, Rotate, Trim/Extend to Corner, Trim/Extend Single Element, Trim/Extend Multiple Elements; Array, Scale, Pin, Unpin, Delete. The status bar says what each tool expects next, and the options bar shows its options. Esc cancels the step in progress; pressed again, it ends the tool.

Move, Copy, Rotate, the two Mirror tools, Array and Scale work on the selection. Started with nothing selected, they let you select first (clicks, Ctrl, windows, Tab), then go on when you press Enter or End on the options bar.

Move, Copy and Rotate also work in 3D views: their points are taken on the plane of the level clicked.

Before each click the tool shows what the click would do: the selection drawn where it would go (moved, copied, turned, mirrored about the axis under the cursor, offset to the cursor's side, aligned to the reference), following the cursor, with the distance or the angle beside it.

Where a tool asks for a second point, you can type a distance (or an angle) instead and press Enter: it shows next to the cursor while you type, and is measured towards the cursor.

docs.title: Move
docs.text:
Click a base point, then the destination. The tool ends and the elements stay selected. Options:

  • Constrain: the move is along or square to the selected wall (horizontal or vertical for other elements);
  • Disjoin: walls joined to the moved ones do not follow, and a door or window can be moved onto another wall;
  • Copy: copies are placed instead; with Multiple, one at each click until Esc.

docs.title: Copy
docs.text: As Move, but a copy is placed. With Multiple, a copy at each click until Esc; Constrain as for Move.

docs.title: Rotate
docs.text: The centre of rotation shows at the middle of the selection; drag it to put it elsewhere. Click the first ray, then the second: the selection turns by the angle between them, shown by a temporary angular dimension. Instead of the second ray, type the angle and press Enter, or type it in Angle on the options bar and press Enter. Copy turns a copy; without Disjoin, walls joined to the turned ones follow.

docs.title: Mirror
docs.text: Mirror - Pick Axis: click a wall, a grid or a line as the axis. Mirror - Draw Axis: click two points. Copy is ticked: a mirrored copy is placed; untick it to mirror the elements themselves.

docs.title: Array
docs.text:
Linear: click two points. Number is how many elements in all. With Move To: 2° the two points give the spacing; with Last, the last element goes to the second point and the others are spread evenly. Constrain keeps the direction along or square to the selection.

Radial: drag the centre where the copies turn about, click the first ray, then the second (or type the angle and press Enter, also in Angle). With 2° the angle is between neighbours, with Last it is the whole span.

docs.title: Offset
docs.text:
Moves a wall or a line square to itself, or places a copy (Copy is ticked).

  • Numerical: set Offset, then click the element on the side it should go to. Press Tab first to offset the whole chain (of the same category) as one: its corners are kept.
  • Graphical: click the element (Tab for the chain), then two points: the distance between them, square to the element, is the offset. You can type it instead. Ctrl copies.

docs.title: Align
docs.text: Click the reference, then the element to align: the face of the element nearest to your click goes onto the face of the reference nearest to its click. Prefer chooses Wall faces or Wall centerlines. After aligning, a padlock shows on the aligned face: click it to keep the two aligned, so that moving the reference moves the other one too. Without Multiple Alignment the next click picks a new reference; with it (or holding Ctrl) you can align several elements to the same one. Esc once starts a new alignment, twice ends the tool.

docs.title: Trim/Extend
docs.text:
Walls and lines are trimmed or extended; click each one on the part to keep.

  • Trim/Extend to Corner: two elements, which then meet at a corner;
  • Trim/Extend Single Element: the boundary, then the element;
  • Trim/Extend Multiple Elements: the boundary, then each element in turn.

docs.title: Split Element and Split with Gap
docs.text: Split Element: click a wall or a line where it should become two. With Delete Inner Segment, click two points: the part between them is removed, with the doors and windows in it. Split with Gap: set Joint Gap, then click: the two parts are that far apart.

docs.title: Scale
docs.text: Walls and lines (and the position of dimensions) can be scaled; with anything else selected, Scale is not available. Graphical: click the origin, the end of a first vector, the end of a second one: the elements are scaled by the ratio of the two lengths (you can type the second one). Numerical: set Scale Factor, then click the origin. Doors and windows keep their distance from the middle of their wall.

docs.title: Pin and Unpin
docs.text: Pin keeps the selected elements where they are: they cannot be dragged, moved by a tool or deleted, and a message says so. A pinned element shows a pushpin when selected; click the pushpin, or use Unpin, to free it.

docs.title: Delete, undo and redo
docs.text: Delete (or the Del key) removes the selection and what it hosts; pinned elements stay. Ctrl+Z undoes the last change and Ctrl+Y redoes it: each tool, drag or nudge is one step.

docs.title: Typed shortcuts
docs.text: Type the letters and press Enter: MV Move, CO Copy, RO Rotate, MM Mirror - Pick Axis, DM Mirror - Draw Axis, AR Array, OF Offset, AL Align, TR Trim/Extend to Corner, SL Split Element, SG Split with Gap, RE Scale. PN pins and UP unpins the selection, SA selects all its instances visible in the view. Keyboard shortcuts lists them all.

docs.title: Not yet available
docs.text:
• Tab to reach a part of an element: a curtain panel or mullion, a part of a stacked wall;
  • Select All Instances from a type in the Project Browser;
  • Group and Associate of Array;
  • splitting walls along a horizontal line in elevations and 3D views;
  • cut, copy and paste through the clipboard, Paste Aligned, Create Similar.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This chapter collects situations that can surprise you, and what to do about them. It grows with the manual: each area of the realignment adds its own.

docs.title: The web app shows «BIMopen non si è avviato» and an error
docs.text:
The browser could not give BIMopen a graphics surface: the message ends with webgl2 not available or with a WebGPU error. BIMopen in the browser needs WebGPU or WebGL2.

  • Turn on hardware acceleration in the settings of the browser, then reload the page.
  • Try another browser, or a newer version of the same one.
  • Add ?webgl to the address to use WebGL2 even where WebGPU exists but does not work.

docs.title: The desktop app does not build on Linux
docs.text:
The interface needs the development files of xkbcommon, Wayland and GTK 3. On Debian and Ubuntu:

sudo apt-get install -y libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libgtk-3-dev

docs.title: The Properties palette, the Project Browser or the command line has disappeared
docs.text: They are closed with the × on their title, or from View ▸ Windows ▸ User Interface. Tick them again in User Interface. The Properties button of the contextual tab also shows the palette again.

docs.title: What I type ends up at the command line
docs.text: Whatever you type while no field is being edited goes to the command line: this is how typed shortcuts work. To type in a field of the Properties palette or of a dialog, click the field first.

docs.title: A button is greyed
docs.text: Some tools work only in the right view, and their tip says why. Area Boundary Line and Area need an open area plan: the tip says Open an area plan first. Save View needs an open 3D view; Sheet Composition ▸ View needs an open sheet; Undo and Redo are greyed when there is nothing to undo or redo.

docs.title: DL starts a dimension instead of a detail line
docs.text: DL is the short form of the linear dimension. To draw detail lines, use Annotate ▸ Detail ▸ Detail line, or type detailline.

docs.title: «no wall at that point»
docs.text: A door or a window must be placed in a wall. Click on the wall itself, or give a point on its line at the command line.

docs.title: A height set at the command line is enormous
docs.text: At the command line a number without unit is in metres: set Unconnected Height 2700 makes the wall 2700 m high. Undo with Ctrl+Z and write the unit: 2700mm or 2.7m. In the Properties palette a number without unit is in the project's units.

docs.title: Unsaved work is gone after New, Open or Sample project
docs.text: These commands replace the current project without asking. Save before using them: the asterisk after the project's name in the title bar shows that there are unsaved changes.

docs.title: Open… in the browser does not show a file dialog
docs.text: In the browser, drag the .bimopen file into the page: the command line says Drag a .bimopen file into the window to open it.

docs.title: bimopen-cli prints its usage and stops
docs.text: The arguments are not the ones it expects: it ends with code 2 and shows the usage. A command that fails ends with code 1 and a message saying which line failed. See Command line and MCP.

docs.title: Views and graphics
docs.text: This chapter describes the views of the model, how each one is drawn, and how to change what a view shows and how: visual styles, scale and detail level, the view range of a plan, crop regions, hiding and isolating, Visibility/Graphics, filters and view templates. Line weights, line patterns and object styles are described in the same terms by the program's dialogs Manage ▸ Settings.

docs.title: 3D views
docs.text:
View ▸ Create ▸ 3D View ▸ Default 3D View opens the default 3D view, {3D}, framing the whole model; opened again, it shows the model as it was left. Drag to orbit (or Shift and the middle button), drag with the middle button to pan, and turn the wheel to zoom at the cursor; see The interface.

To keep a framing, View ▸ Create ▸ 3D View ▸ Save View: type a name and press Enter. The new view is listed under 3D Views in the Project Browser and opens at once; it keeps the framing it is left with. Renaming {3D} in the Project Browser (right-click ▸ Rename…) does the same: {3D} becomes a named view, and the next default 3D view is a new {3D}.

A selected element is washed in blue and half see-through, its edges in blue: what is behind it stays visible.

Floors cut the walls they pass through: where a slab crosses a wall the wall stops under it and goes on above it, so the slab's edge and the wall's face are one surface.

docs.title: Visual styles
docs.text:
The Visual Style button of the view control bar, at the bottom of every view window, offers:

Style What is drawn Wireframe Every edge, also those behind other faces; no faces Hidden Line Faces in the paper colour and the edges in front of them Shaded Faces lit, in the colour of their material Shaded with Edges As Shaded, with the edges in front Consistent Colors Faces in the colour of their material, the same whatever the light

The style belongs to the view and can be undone. The keyboard shortcuts WF, HL and SD choose Wireframe, Hidden Line and Shaded.

The edges are the real ones: where two faces meet at an angle, and the outline of each face and each opening. A wall with a window shows its own outline and the window's, and no line where the pieces of the wall meet.

Plans, sections and elevations have a visual style too. A plan is drawn in Hidden Line until another style is chosen; in Shaded its floors, seen from above, take the colour of their material, and the faces of sections and elevations take their materials' colours.

docs.title: Sun and shadows
docs.text:
In a 3D view the view control bar has two more buttons:

  • Shadows On / Shadows Off: in the shaded styles the sun lights the model and casts shadows, from the walls onto the floors, from the roof's eaves onto the walls;
  • the sun path button: Sun Path On draws a compass ring on the ground around the model, with the four points of the compass, the sun's path through the day as an arc over it, and the sun where it is. Sun Settings… sets where the sun is:
Mode What it takes Still Latitude, Longitude, Time zone (UTC), the day and month and the Time: the sun's position follows Lighting Azimuth (degrees clockwise from north) and Altitude

Each view has its own sun settings, and the changes can be undone. Shadows are drawn by the 3D window on the graphics card; plans, sections, elevations and exported images do not show them yet.

docs.title: Plans and their view range
docs.text:
View ▸ Create ▸ Plan Views ▸ Floor Plan opens New Plan: pick the levels and the scale, then OK. With Do not duplicate existing views on, the levels that already have a plan are left out; turn it off to make a second plan of a level.

A plan is a horizontal cut of the model at the Cut Plane of its view range. Walls crossing the cut plane are drawn cut, with the cut patterns of their layers' materials at Medium and Fine detail; lower walls and the floors of the level are seen from above.

To change the view range, select nothing (so that Properties shows the view), then View range ▸ Edit…. Each plane is measured from a level, with an offset:

Plane Level Top The plan's own level (Associated Level), the Level Above, a level by name, or Unlimited Cut Plane Always the plan's own level Bottom The plan's own level, the Level Below or a level by name View Depth As Bottom, or Unlimited

OK sets the four planes together, as one change. They must stay in order, from the top down (top, cut plane, bottom, view depth): otherwise the window explains what is wrong and stays open. Floors below the bottom, down to the view depth, are drawn beyond in thin lines; so are floors a little under the bottom, such as a sunken slab, even with the view depth at the bottom.

docs.title: Light and dark background
docs.text: Options ▸ Theme ▸ Dark (or Invert background color) turns the drawing area dark. As on an inverted background, black lines, text and patterns are drawn light, colours keep their hue, and colour fills such as the rooms' are darkened, so the text over them stays readable. Options ▸ Interface size makes the whole interface bigger, from 100 % to 250 %, on top of the screen's own scale: useful on screens with many pixels. It is kept for the next start.

docs.title: Opening a view from its symbol
docs.text: Double-click a view's symbol to open its view: a section line or its head, an elevation symbol, a callout's boundary (a reference callout opens the view it points at), a level's line in a section or elevation (its floor plan opens), or a view placed on a sheet. The view's window becomes the active one.

docs.title: Scale, detail level and crop region
docs.text:
The view control bar shows the view's View Scale and Detail Level (in 3D views too).

  • At a smaller scale the model is drawn smaller on paper while text, tags and symbols keep their size on paper: at 1:200 a text covers twice as much of the model as at 1:100.
  • At Coarse a cut wall is one fill; at Medium and Fine its layers show, each with its material.

Sections cut the model the same way. Walls, floors and roofs that meet in the cut are drawn as one: a thick outline round them, a thin line only where two materials meet, none between two parts of the same material; walls attached to a roof stop under it. Each cut layer has its material's cut pattern (at Coarse, the type's Coarse Scale Fill Pattern in its Coarse Scale Fill Color, set on wall, floor and roof types, else one solid fill). Furniture and plumbing fixtures are never cut: they are seen whole. A window is cut with its frame in the thick cut line and its glass in thin lines; what lies beyond the cut is drawn in thinner projection lines.

Crop View clips the view to its crop region, Show Crop Region draws the region; drag its edges to resize it. To type its size: Properties ▸ Size Crop ▸ Edit…, then Width and Height; the region keeps its centre.

docs.title: Hiding and isolating
docs.text:
Temporary Hide/Isolate (the glasses on the view control bar) acts on the selected elements, in the active view only, and does not change the project:

Command Shortcut What stays visible Isolate Element HI Only the selected elements Hide Element HH Everything but the selected elements Isolate Category IC Only the categories of the selected elements Hide Category HC Everything but those categories

The view gets a coloured border. Each use narrows what is shown: hiding one element and then another hides both. Reset Temporary Hide/Isolate (HR) shows everything again; Apply Hide/Isolate to View hides for good what was hidden for now.

To hide for good in the view, select the elements, then right-click ▸ Hide in view ▸ Elements or Category, or the contextual tab's View ▸ Hide in View, or type EH (elements) or VH (category).

Reveal Hidden Elements (the light bulb on the view control bar, or RH) frames the view in magenta and shows what is hidden in magenta, the rest in halftone. A hidden element can then be selected and shown again: right-click ▸ Unhide in View ▸ Elements (or Category). Click the light bulb again, or type RH, to leave.

docs.title: Visibility/Graphics
docs.text:
View ▸ Graphics ▸ Visibility/Graphics (or VG, or Properties ▸ Visibility/graphics overrides ▸ Edit…) shows, for the active view, one row per category:

  • the check box shows or hides the category; Show model categories in this view shows or hides them all;
  • Projection lines and Cut lines: Override… sets the weight, colour and pattern;
  • Surface Patterns and Cut Patterns: the material's patterns, hidden, in another colour or replaced by another fill pattern;
  • Halftone blends the lines with the background;
  • Transparent makes the surfaces see-through in the 3D view;
  • Detail Level draws the category at another level than the view.

Clear overrides takes the selected rows back to the object styles. Changes show at once: Apply keeps them and the window, Cancel (or the window's ×) takes back what was not applied, OK keeps them and closes.

One element can have its own graphics in a view: select it, then right-click ▸ Override graphics in view ▸ By Element… (or the contextual tab's View panel). View-Specific Element Graphics has Visible, Halftone, Transparent, the surface and cut patterns and the projection and cut lines. They apply only in this view, over the category's and the filters'.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
View ▸ Graphics ▸ Filters lists the project's filters: New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete. A filter has categories and up to four rules on their parameters, all of which an element must meet.

In Visibility/Graphics ▸ Filters, Add applies a filter to the view; its row then sets visibility, lines, Halftone and Transparent for the elements that pass it. Where filters disagree, the one higher in the list wins: Up and Down move the selected filter.

docs.title: View templates
docs.text: View ▸ Graphics ▸ View templates ▸ Create template from current view keeps the view's scale, detail level, visual style, view range and graphics as a template, by name. View templates ▸ Apply template to current view gives them to another view of the same kind: a plan (a second plan of a level too), a section or elevation, or a 3D view. A view does not follow later changes of its template until it is applied again, and the graphics of single elements are never part of a template.

docs.title: Managing views
docs.text:
Right-click a view in the Project Browser:

  • Duplicate View ▸ Duplicate copies the view with its properties; Duplicate with Detailing copies its dimensions, text, tags and 2D details too. The copy opens;
  • Rename… asks for the new name (Rename View); names stay unique among views.

View ▸ Windows ▸ Tile shows all the open views side by side, filling the drawing area: with three windows, the active one on the left at full height and two stacked on the right.

docs.title: Walls, doors and windows
docs.text: This chapter describes how walls are drawn, how they join and attach to roofs and floors, how their types and layers are set up, and how doors and windows are placed in them, flipped, moved and drawn at each detail level.

docs.title: Drawing walls
docs.text:
Home ▸ Build ▸ Wall (or type WA) starts the wall tool, in a plan or in the 3D view. Pick the wall type in the type selector at the top of the Properties palette; Type Properties changes the type, and with it every wall of that type. The contextual tab Edit | Place Wall shows the Draw panel, and the options bar shows:

Option What it does Height or Depth The wall rises from the level (Height) or goes down from it (Depth) A level, or Unconnected with a value The wall reaches that level, or is that high (or deep) Level In a 3D view only: the level the walls stand on; takes the level of the surface of the first click Location Line The plane of the wall that runs along the clicks: Wall Centerline (the default), the core centre line, or one of the finish and core faces, exterior or interior Chain On, each click ends a wall and starts the next one; off, each two clicks make a wall on its own Offset The location line runs this far from the clicks, towards the exterior Radius Not available: it needs curved walls, and is shown disabled

In the 3D view the wall being drawn follows the cursor as a solid, with its thickness and its height up to the top level (or the height typed), on the plane of the level, with its length and angle as a temporary dimension; Shift keeps it square and Esc takes it away.

While drawing:

  • the wall's exterior is on the left of the drawing direction: drawn from left to right, the exterior face is at the top. The preview shows the exterior face thicker;
  • the space bar puts the exterior of the next wall on the other side;
  • after the first point, type a length and press Enter: the wall ends that far, in the direction of the cursor;
  • Esc ends the chain; Esc again, or Modify, ends the tool.

The Draw panel picks the shape:

Shape How Line Click the start and the end of each wall Rectangle Click two opposite corners: four joined walls, with the exterior outside Inscribed Polygon Set Sides in the options bar, click the centre and a corner: the corners are on the circle Circumscribed Polygon The same, but the sides touch the circle Pick Lines Click a line of the plan (a line or an edge of an element): a wall along it. Press TAB over a line to take the whole chain of lines joined to it, then click

docs.title: The location line and flipping
docs.text: Select a wall: blue dots mark the ends of its location line, and two arrows stand on its exterior side. Clicking the arrows turns the wall over about its location line: the first and the last layers swap, and the doors and windows keep their orientation. Changing Location Line of a placed wall does not move it; the next flip turns it about the new plane. Changing the type of a wall, or its layers, keeps its location line where it was.

docs.title: Attaching walls to roofs and floors
docs.text:
A wall can follow a roof or a floor instead of a fixed height.

  1. Select the walls.
  2. Edit | Walls ▸ Modify Wall ▸ Attach Top/Base.
  3. In the options bar, Attach Wall: Top or Base.
  4. Click the roof or floor, in a plan, a section or the 3D view.

With Top, the walls rise or drop to the underside of the roof (following its slopes: the gable walls go up to the ridge) or of the floor above. With Base, they stand on the top face of the floor below. From then on they follow it: a steeper roof, a roof raised by its base offset, a moved floor carry the walls with them.

To detach them: select the walls, Edit | Walls ▸ Modify Wall ▸ Detach Top/Base, then click the element to detach them from, or press Detach All in the options bar. The walls keep the height they have at that moment, and can be attached again at any time. When a roof or floor with walls attached to it is deleted, the walls keep their height too.

The properties Top is Attached and Base is Attached show the state (read-only); while the top is attached, Unconnected Height is read-only.

docs.title: Editing a wall's profile
docs.text:
A wall need not be a rectangle: its outline can be sketched in an elevation or a section parallel to it, with holes, as for a gable or a stepped wall.

  1. Select the wall and click Mode ▸ Edit Profile in its contextual tab. From a plan or a view that is not parallel to the wall, Go To View lists the sections and elevations parallel to it: choose one and click Open View.
  2. Sketch mode opens with the wall's outline in magenta. Change it with Line and Rectangle (see sketch mode): pick a line and press Del, draw new ones; a loop inside is a hole.
  3. Click Finish Edit Mode (or Cancel Edit Mode to leave the wall as it was).

The wall takes that outline in 3D, in sections and in plan, where it is cut only where the outline reaches the cut plane; its doors and windows still cut it. A top attached to a roof or a floor still clips it. A curtain wall keeps the panels and mullions inside its new outline. Mode ▸ Reset Profile makes it a rectangle again; Ctrl+Z undoes either.

The profile can also be edited in the 3D view: the sketch lies on the wall's plane and the view stays 3D. Only from a plan does Go To View appear, and nothing changes until a view is opened with Open View. While sketching, the wall's original outline is drawn as dashed reference lines; the sketch snaps to their ends and onto them.

docs.title: Wall joins
docs.text:
Walls whose ends meet join by themselves, and so do a wall ending on the side of another and two walls crossing each other. At Medium and Fine detail each layer is resolved against the layers of the other wall:

  • at a corner (an L), each layer meets the same layer of the other wall: the finishes wrap round the corner and the cores meet;
  • at a T, the core of the wall that ends runs through the finishes of the other wall up to its core; its own finishes stop at the face, which is open there;
  • where two walls cross (an X), a core runs through the finishes of the other wall;
  • pieces of the same material merge with no line between them; a thin line separates two different materials; the free outline is drawn thick.

At Coarse detail joined walls are one fill, with no line between them. Sections and the 3D view use the same pieces, so nothing overlaps.

docs.title: The Wall Joins tool
docs.text:
Edit ▸ Geometry ▸ Wall Joins, then click the grey square that appears on a corner. The options bar offers:

  • Configuration: Butt (one wall runs through, the other stops against it), Miter (both end on the bisector) or Square off (the wall that stops ends square); Previous and Next change which wall runs through;
  • Display: Clean Join, Don't Clean Join (the walls butt, with a thick line between them) or Use View Setting.

Each change can be undone. Esc ends the tool.

The plan's property Wall Join Display (in Graphics) is the view setting: Clean all wall joins, or Clean same wall type to keep a thick line where walls of two types meet, unless their corner is set to Clean Join.

docs.title: Disallowing a join
docs.text: To keep an end of a wall from joining (an expansion gap, say), select the wall, right-click the blue dot of that end and choose Disallow Join: both walls then end square, apart. A small mark beside the end shows it; click it, or right-click the dot and choose Allow Join, to join it again.

docs.title: Wall types and layers
docs.text:
Type Properties of a wall shows, under Construction, Structure with its Edit… button, Wrapping at Inserts, Wrapping at Ends, Width (the sum of the layers, read-only) and Function (Interior, Exterior, Foundation, Retaining, Soffit, Core-shaft); under Graphics, Coarse Scale Fill Pattern and Coarse Scale Fill Color, how cut walls of the type are filled at Coarse detail. Duplicate… makes a new type; its name does not follow its layers.

Structure ▸ Edit… opens Edit assembly: the layers from the exterior side to the interior side, each with its function, material and thickness, between the two Core Boundary rows. Insert, Delete, Up and Down change the list. A membrane layer has no thickness, and every other layer is at least 4 mm thick: other values are refused, and the dialog stays open.

The Wraps column ticks the layers that may wrap. Below the table:

  • Wrapping at Inserts (Do not wrap, Exterior, Interior, Both): the ticked layers outside the core on that side turn into the jambs of doors and windows; the layers behind them are pulled back;
  • Wrapping at Ends (Do not wrap, Exterior, Interior): the same at the free ends of the walls.

Wrapping is drawn in plan only. A door or window type overrides the wall's wrapping with its Wall Closure.

docs.title: Wall properties
docs.text: Under Constraints: Location Line, Base Constraint, Base Offset, Base is Attached, Top Constraint (a level, or Unconnected), Unconnected Height, Top Offset (with a level), Top is Attached and Room Bounding (untick it and the rooms around the wall ignore it). Under Dimensions: Length, Area, Volume. Under Identity Data: Mark and Comments.

docs.title: Placing doors and windows
docs.text:
Home ▸ Build ▸ Door (DR) or Window (WN), in a plan, a section, an elevation or the 3D view. Pick the type, then move over a wall: the opening follows the cursor along it, and temporary dimensions measure from its centre line to the centre lines of the nearest walls across the host on each side. A door swings to the side of the wall the cursor is on; the space bar puts its hinge on the other jamb. Click to place it: the wall is cut in every view. A window takes its type's Default Sill Height.

Doors and windows get a Mark that counts up by category (1, 2, 3…), from the highest.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Edit | Place Door ▸ Tag ▸ Tag on Placement (or the same for windows) tags each opening as it is placed. The options bar then offers Horizontal or Vertical, and Leader with its length. A door's tag shows its Mark; a window's tag shows its type's Type Mark. Annotate ▸ Tag All tags the openings not tagged yet.

docs.title: Flipping a door or window
docs.text: Select a door or window in a plan: arrows across the wall, on the side it opens to, turn its swing over; arrows beside it, along the wall, put its hinge on the other jamb. The context menu does the same: Flip Hand (the hinge) and Flip Facing (the swing).

docs.title: Moving a door or window to another wall
docs.text: Select it, Edit | Doors ▸ Host ▸ Pick New Host (or Edit | Windows), then click another wall: the opening moves there, where you clicked, with its type and sill. It stays selected.

docs.title: Door and window properties
docs.text:
Instance: Level, Sill Height, Width and Height (of the type), Head Height, Comments, Mark. Changing Sill Height or Head Height moves the opening up or down; its size stays.

Type: Wall Closure (By host, or a wrapping of its own), Function (Interior or Exterior), Door Material (Glass Material for windows) and Frame Material, Trim Width, Thickness (of a door's leaf, or the depth of a window's frame), Default Sill Height and Window Inset (windows: how far the frame sits from the exterior face), Trim Projection Ext and Trim Projection Int (doors), Leaves and Type Mark. A door cannot become a window by changing its type.

docs.title: How walls, doors and windows are drawn
docs.text:
The Detail Level of the plan decides:

Coarse Medium Fine Walls One fill (or the type's coarse pattern), joined walls merged Each layer with its material's cut pattern As Medium Windows The frame as one outline, the glass along it, the wall below seen as lines The frame cut at each jamb and at the mullion of a two-leaf window, at its inset; one line of glass; the exterior sill and the interior sill board As Medium, with double glass Doors The leaf as a line and its swing The frame at each jamb, the leaf with its thickness, its swing As Medium, with the trims out of the faces

In every case the layers end at the jambs of the opening, closed by the cut line, or wrap into them as the types ask. In sections and in 3D, doors and windows show their frame, leaves, glass and sills, in the type's materials.

docs.title: Curtain walls
docs.text:
A curtain wall is a wall of a curtain wall type, drawn with the Wall tool: pick Curtain Wall (one glass panel the length of the wall), Exterior Glazing (grid lines by the type) or Storefront (grid lines and mullions) in the type selector, then draw as for any wall, in plan or in 3D, with Chain and the Draw shapes. A basic wall changes into a curtain wall by picking a curtain wall type in the type selector; the doors and windows it hosts are deleted, because a curtain wall does not host them, and a message says so (undo brings them back).

In plan each glass panel is drawn with its thickness and the mullions are cut. A type with Automatically Embed ticked (the Storefront) drawn along a wall cuts its own hole in it, in plan, sections, 3D and IFC.

  • The type's Vertical Layout and horizontal layout (Fixed distance, Fixed number, Maximum spacing) with their spacing, and the instance's Number of Vertical Grids and Vertical Justification, place the grid lines by themselves.
  • Home ▸ Build ▸ Curtain Grid: click near the top or bottom edge for a vertical line, near a side for a horizontal one, in an elevation, a section or a plan; it snaps to the middle and the thirds of the panel.
  • Home ▸ Build ▸ Mullion: Grid Line, Grid Line Segment or All Grid Lines, with the mullion type picked in the type selector.
  • Select the curtain wall, then Panel in its contextual tab: pick a panel type (a Curtain Wall Door, a glazed or solid panel, or none) and click the panel to change.

Panels and mullions have their own schedules, and the IFC export writes the curtain wall with its plates and members.

docs.title: At the command line
docs.text:
The same operations, typed:

attach                      attach the selected walls to the roof over them
attach 412                  attach their top to element 412 (a roof or a floor)
attach base 398             attach their base to the floor 398
detach all                  detach them from everything
walljoin 0,0 {"kind":"Giunto d'angolo","cleanup":"Non calcolare unioni"}
walljoin 57 1 disallow      wall 57 does not join at its end
rehost 120 12,4             move door or window 120 into the wall at 12,4
door {"point":[3,0],"tag":{"vertical":true,"leader":true,"length":1}}

docs.title: Not available yet
docs.text: Curved walls (Arc, Circle, Radius), Pick Faces, structural walls, stacked walls, wall sweeps and reveals, vertically compound layers (regions), Join Geometry, phases, and skylights in roofs.
